clips.text: How long did she wait?
clips.script: [delighted, leaning in] How long did she WAIT?

clips.text: I'm going to stand over here, on the part of the sidewalk that still has a color.
clips.script: [mellow, polite] i'm going to stand over here, [mellow, laid-back, low-key, calm, firm] on the part of the sidewalk that still has a color.

clips.text: That's new. I need a new color for fire.
clips.script: [thoughtful, intrigued] That's new. [scribbling, matter-of-fact] I need a new color for FIRE.

clips.text: That's the first bread out of me since 1963. Don't stand there looking at it. Cut it.
clips.script: [gruff, moved but hiding it] That's the first bread out of me since nineteen sixty-three. [brusque, covering] Don't stand there looking at it. [gruff] Cut it.

clips.text: White sedan. 8:42. Yes.
clips.script: [clipped, flat] White sedan. [crisp] Eight forty-two. [satisfied] Yes.

clips.text: Girls, behind me. You three have till I count to three. Then I'm getting the hose.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, clipped, in charge] Girls, behind me. [warm Long Island accent, low, slow, almost polite] You three have till I count to three. Then I'm getting the HOSE.

clips.text: He's stuck! Tata, get him out!
clips.script: [worried for him, loud] He's STUCK! [demanding] Tata, get him out!

clips.text: It was inside a block all day.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, dry, incredulous] It was inside a block all DAY.

clips.text: The fish gets THREE?
clips.script: [thick New York accent, hurt, baffled, louder than before, punchline] The FISH gets THREE?

clips.text: She doesn't have a basement. She has that shed with the two padlocks.
clips.script: [helpful, joining in] She doesn't have a basement. [conspiratorial, low] She has that shed with the TWO padlocks.

clips.text: That's what I don't like about it. The dough rises. The dog jumps. That thing is just waiting.
clips.script: [mellow, uneasy] that's what i don't like about it. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, low, thoughtful] the dough rises. the dog jumps. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, quiet, ominous] that thing is just waiting.

clips.text: The man rented a car AT THE AIRPORT. That means he flies back and forth. Like you. The next one is here. Come home.
clips.script: [urgent, triumphant] The man rented a car AT THE AIRPORT. [sharp, working it out] That means he flies back and forth. [pointed] Like YOU. [serious, firm] The next one is here. [quiet, plain] Come home.

clips.text: I know what it is. It's my pension. Sixty years late, and a little flame carried it in this morning.
clips.script: [gruff, certain] I know what it is. [proud, flat] It's my PENSION. [gruff, vindicated] Sixty years late, and a little flame carried it in this morning.

clips.text: Give the niece my number, 3468. And don't get ideas. I'm not being friendly. She keeps records, and I respect records.
clips.script: [gruff, dismissive] Give the niece my number, three four six eight. [warning, sharp] And don't get ideas. [flat, firm] I'm not being friendly. [dry, matter-of-fact] She keeps records, and I respect RECORDS.

clips.text: Three.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, flat, immediate, punchline] Three.

clips.text: Your face is RED, Tata!
clips.script: [delighted] Your face is RED, Tata!

clips.text: Hold on. This is the Car Barn loaf. My father brought one home every morning until they shut that place. Who baked this?
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, slow, stopped short] Hold on. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, quiet, wondering] This is the Car Barn loaf. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, soft, remembering] My father brought one home every morning until they shut that place. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, gruff, asking] Who baked this?

clips.text: Girls, you heard that. Forty minutes. Somebody watch the clock.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, gleeful, showman] Girls, you heard that. FORTY minutes. Somebody watch the clock.

clips.text: That's your whole rosebush. It's inside an orange block the size of a minivan.
clips.script: [stunned, plain] That's your whole rosebush. [flat, amazed] It's inside an orange block the size of a MINIVAN.

clips.text: Is that the chart? It has a key. It's color coded. That's the wall the detective has right before they take his badge away.
clips.script: [mellow, impressed] is that the chart? it has a key. it's color coded. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, delighted] that's the wall the detective has right before they take his badge away.
